stories.headline: ‘Most likely fake’, says Telangana DGP on email threatening 26/11 like terror attack
stories.title: ‘Most likely fake’, says Telangana DGP on email threatening 26/11 like terror attack
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'terror attack' in title weight 84
article_sentences: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links.

Hyderabad police intensified security across the city after receiving an email threatening bomb blasts at two prominent locations – Hotel Tourist Plaza in Kacheguda and Kacheguda Railway Station – and warning of a 26/11-style terror attack.
Although officials suspect the message to be a hoax, security arrangements have been tightened as a precaution.
The threat email, received on November 21, was reportedly sent by a person claiming links to the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT).
The sender allegedly threatened to target the hotel and railway station, claiming the attacks would kill at least 300 people.
Responding to the email, Telangana Director General of Police (DGP) CV Anand said that the prima facie evidence pointed to the mail being fake.
He however also said that officials are following Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) regarding the issue.

The email had also threatened to replicate the November 26, 2008, Mumbai terror attacks in Hyderabad to avenge the killing of LeT operative Lateef Bhat and his associates by the Indian Army in Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir.

Following the alert issued by the Special Branch, police personnel across Hyderabad were directed to strengthen security at the two locations and step up surveillance at crowded public spaces, including hotels, railway stations, bus stations, religious places and other key installations.
Anti-sabotage checks were carried out at the locations named in the email and other sensitive areas.
Police said no explosives were found during the searches.
Patrolling and visible policing have also been increased, while personnel have been instructed to watch out for suspicious individuals, unattended objects and vehicles.

stories.headline: Kerala Literature Festival promises much for book lovers as it returns after pandemic
stories.title: Kerala Literature Festival promises much for book lovers as it returns after pandemic
stories.summary: Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan to open the event on Kozhikode beach on Thursday

article_sentences: It has not taken the Kerala Literature Festival (KLF) long to earn a prominent place in the State’s cultural landscape.
After a three-year break, necessitated by the pandemic, the KLF is back in the physical world (it was held online in 2021).
The sixth edition will get under way on the Kozhikode beach on Thursday.
It promises plenty for the book lovers of Malabar and beyond over the next four years.

Writers such as Shehan Karunatilaka, who won the Booker Prize three months ago, Arundhati Roy, Shashi Tharoor, Nobel laureates Ada Yonath and Abhijit Banerjee, historians William Dalrymple, Yuval Noah Harari, Ramachandra Guha, Manu S. Pillai, actors Kamal Haasan, Prakash Raj, Mukesh, and Indrans are among those who will speak at sessions that will deal with a variety of topics.
Around 500 speakers, including those from countries such as the United States, UK, Spain, Israel, and New Zealand, will speak in 248 sessions, in fact.
“This is going to be the biggest edition of the KFL yet,” the festival’s chief facilitator.
Ravi Deecee told The Hindu.
“In 2020, the footfall for the festival was around three lakh.
We expect that number to go up to four or five lakh this time,” he added.
He said he was glad that the festival had evolved as something that was not just literature.
“For instance, we have been able to line up several prominent economists this time around.

stories.title: India's ties with Russia can help push for end to Ukraine war: Dutch FM

Berendsen is on an official visit to India from November 22 to 23. He co-chaired the inaugural Foreign Ministers' Meeting with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi on Sunday and reviewed the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership. "We actually see it as an added value of our relationship with India that it has a relationship with Russia and can also use that relation to show Russia that it needs to put an end to this war and accept a ceasefire," he said. The Russia-Ukraine war, in its fifth year, continues with intensified attacks

stories.headline: St Theressa Institute students visit Usman War Memorial along LoC
stories.title: St Theressa Institute students visit Usman War Memorial along LoC
stories.summary: Rajouri, Nov 22: Jhangar Battalion of the Indian Army organised an educational visit for around 200 students of St Theressa Institute of Education, Rajouri, to the Usman War Memorial located along the Line of Control (LoC). The visit aimed at familiarising students with the military history of the region and inspiring them through the courage, leadership and sacrifices of soldiers who defended the nation. During the visit, students were briefed about the “Battle of Nowshera”, fought during the 1947-48 Indo-Pak conflict. They were informed about the challenging circumstances faced by the Indian Army and the determined resistance offered by troops to defend Nowshera and adjoining areas. Special emphasis was laid on the role of Brigadier Mohammad Usman, popularly known as the 'Lion of Nowshera'. Students were apprised of his exemplary leadership, courage and ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty while defending the strategic Nowshera sector. They were also briefed about the historical significance of the Usman War Memorial and the importance of preserving the legacy of soldiers who laid down their lives in the service of the nation. The interaction highlighted values of discipline, courage, perseverance, leadership and selfless service, while encouraging students to learn from history and become responsible citizens. Organised under the theme 'Know Your History, Be Inspired for Tomorrow', the initiative provided students an opportunity to experience history beyond textbooks and develop a deeper understanding of the sacrifices made by the Armed Forces. “The visit was part of Jhangar Battalion's continued efforts to connect with the local community, promote awareness about the region's military heritage and inspire younger generations through stories of valour and sacrifice,” the Army spokesperson said.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan disrupts fishing in Tamil Nadu's Tuticorin; fishermen seek Rs 5,000 assistance
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan disrupts fishing in Tamil Nadu's Tuticorin; fishermen seek Rs 5,000 assistance
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu): Over 200 mechanised fishing boats from Tuticorin ventured into the sea early on Monday after a 10-day break triggered by Cyclone Akvan, even as fishermen urged the Tamil Nadu government to provide Rs 5,000 in relief to tide over the monsoon-induced lean period.
Following an India Meteorological Department warning of strong winds over the sea due to Cyclone Akvan, the Tuticorin district.
Fisheries Department had barred fishermen from venturing into the waters from November 13 until further notice.
After the restriction was lifted, country-boat and fibre-boat fishermen resumed operations on November 20.
Mechanised boat operators, however, remained ashore for 10 days before setting sail early Monday from the Tuticorin Mechanised Boat Fishing Harbour.
With fishing resuming after a 10-day gap, fishermen expressed optimism that the catch would be good.
Highlighting the recurring impact of the northeast monsoon, fishermen noted that rough seas and cyclonic systems between October and December steadily reduce their working days every year.
In November alone, they were forced to stay off the sea for 17 days, severely affecting their livelihoods.

Fishermen urged the state government to enhance the financial assistance extended during the May fishing ban and lean fishing periods, and provide an additional Rs 5,000 to cover the three-month monsoon lean season.

A fishermen's representative told PTI Videos that it has become extremely difficult to venture into the sea even for 150 days out of 365 in a year, given cyclones, floods, and the mandatory 60-day annual fishing ban.

Urging the government to intervene and hike the relief amount this year itself, the representative sought an immediate allocation of Rs 5,000 for the November–December period to support families facing severe hardship.
Tuticorin is a major fishing harbour, with over 20,000 people depending directly on the sector and another 10,000 indirectly for their livelihoods.

stories.headline: CPI(M) Accuses BJP of Violating Tripura Poll Rules Over Election Pamphlets, Posters
stories.title: CPI(M) Accuses BJP of Violating Tripura Poll Rules Over Election Pamphlets, Posters
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: AGARTALA: The CPI(M) has alleged that the ruling BJP is violating the election code of conduct and urged the State Election Commission to take appropriate action.

The party claimed that the pamphlets and posters being used by the BJP for its election campaign did not carry the mandatory declaration of the printer and publisher, as required under the Tripura Municipal (Conduct of Election) Rules, 1995.
The complaint was filed by CPI(M) state secretary Jitendra Chaudhury, who demanded an immediate halt to the distribution of the pamphlets and legal action against the concerned printer and publisher.
According to the complaint, BJP workers had been distributing the pamphlets door-to-door while campaigning in various municipal and nagar panchayat areas ahead of the November 27 polls.

The pamphlets reportedly carried photographs and appeals from Chief Minister Manik Saha, BJP state president Abhishek Debray and MP Biplab Kumar Deb, along with the party's election symbol and an appeal to vote for the BJP.
Chaudhury cited sub-rule (1) of Rule 95 of the 1995 rules, which bars the printing or publication of election material without the mandatory declaration.
He also alleged that several flexes, posters, hoardings and banners featuring BJP candidates across Agartala lacked the required details of the printer and publisher.
Citing sub-rule (4) of the same rule, Chaudhury said violations attracted imprisonment of up to six months, a fine of up to Rs 2,000, or both.
He called for strict enforcement of the election rules to ensure free and fair polls.

stories.headline: PM Modi's Gold Appeal: Foreign Exchange Savings, Gold Prices & Congress-Shastri Row
stories.title: PM Modi's Gold Appeal: Foreign Exchange Savings, Gold Prices & Congress-Shastri Row
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has credited citizens for responding to his appeal to avoid unnecessary gold purchases, as gold prices take a dip. Speaking at the National Skill Convocation in Lucknow, the PM said public cooperation could help conserve India's foreign exchange reserves amid global economic and energy uncertainties. The appeal, first made in Hyderabad in May, has also received backing from traders' bodies and Union Minister Piyush Goyal. But Modi's comparison with former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri's appeal to give up one meal a week during the 1965 war has triggered a political controversy, with Congress MP Imran Masood questioning the comparison. Did the appeal help India's economy, or has it become another political flashpoint?

Midcap IT stocks Coforge and Persistent Systems gained 2.5% and 2%, respectively. stories.title: Supreme Court Suspends Sentence Of Godhra Train Burning Convict On Medical Grounds
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(November 23) suspended the sentence of Irfan Siraj Pada, one of the convicts in the Godhra train burning case.
It granted bail to him on medical grounds and considering that he has been in custody for more than 17 years.
A bench comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale passed an order considering that Irfan suffers from serious cardiovascular disease.
The State did not dispute the medical condition of the convict.
The crime which took place on February 27, 2002, resulted in the killing of 58 persons in a fire inside the S-6 coach of the Sabarmati Express, which was carrying kar sevaks from Ayodhya.
The Godhra carnage triggered communal riots in Gujarat.
In March 2011, the trial court had convicted 31 persons, of whom 11 were sentenced to death and the remaining 20 awarded life in prison.
63 other accused were acquitted.
In 2017, the Gujarat High Court commuted the death sentence of 11 to life-term and upheld the life sentence awarded to the other 20.
The appeals filed by the convicts in the Supreme Court have been pending since 2018.

On May 13, 2022, the Court had granted one of the convicts, Abdul Raheman Dhantiya @ Kankatto @Jamburo, interim bail for six months on the ground that his wife was suffering from terminal cancer and that his daughters were mentally challenged.
On November 11, 2022, the Court extended his bail till March 31, 2023.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Dismisses PIL Seeking Corrections In UP Municipal Electoral Rolls
stories.title: Supreme Court Dismisses PIL Seeking Corrections In UP Municipal Electoral Rolls
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a public interest litigation (PIL) that sought corrections to municipal electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh over alleged discrepancies in house numbers.
A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana declined to entertain the plea.
Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed that the right to seek correction of an electoral-roll entry is personal to the individual voter and cannot ordinarily be pursued collectively through a PIL.
“You are moving this petition as a public interest litigation.
The right to correct an electoral roll is personal.
In your municipal list also, there will be certain rules.
Let the individuals approach.
But on a collective basis, it can only be when it is done across the State.
Voters can take it up.
Individual voters can come to us,” Justice Bagchi said.
The Court noted that municipal electoral rolls are governed by their own set of rules and that individual voters can approach the competent election authorities for necessary corrections.

The petitioner had contended that house numbers had changed in several areas, that representations made in this regard remained unaddressed, and that municipal electoral rolls should be aligned with those prepared for parliamentary and assembly elections.

stories.summary: Tata Steel shares fell nearly 5% after it agreed to acquire up to 26.38% of APL Apollo Tubes for about ₹15,511 crore and announced a public offer for another 26%. If both transactions are completed, Tata Steel could own 52.38% of the company and expand its downstream steel business.

article_sentences: Tata Steel shares fell over 5% on Monday, 23 November, after the steelmaker announced plans to acquire a controlling stake in structural steel tubes manufacturer APL Apollo Tubes for approximately ₹15,511 crore, alongside a mandatory open offer that could involve another ₹16,756 crore.
The proposed acquisition marks a major strategic shift for Tata Steel as it looks to strengthen its presence in higher-margin, value-added steel products and expand its downstream business.
Under a share purchase agreement signed with promoter group entity S Gupta Holding Pvt.
Ltd., Tata Steel will acquire up to 7.38 crore equity shares of APL Apollo, representing 26.38% of its expanded voting share capital, at ₹2,100 per share.
The transaction involves a total cash consideration of approximately ₹15,510.61 crore.
The acquisition of the promoter stake will be completed in three phases.
In the first tranche, Tata Steel is acquiring 2.77 crore shares, representing a 9.91% stake, through an on-market block deal on Monday.
The remaining acquisition will take place through two off-market transfers.
These comprise 3.33 crore shares, or an 11.9% stake, and another 1.28 crore shares, representing 4.57%.
The transfers are expected to be completed on or before 31 March 2028, subject to regulatory approvals and fulfilment of closing conditions.

Following the acquisition of the promoter stake, Tata Steel has triggered mandatory takeover provisions and announced an open offer to acquire up to 7.28 crore additional equity shares, representing 26% of APL Apollo's share capital, from public shareholders.
The open offer has been priced at ₹2,301.40 per share and could entail an additional cash outlay of up to ₹16,755.66 crore if fully subscribed.

article_sentences: Indore Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri has said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s policies insulated Indian consumers from global fuel price shocks, underscoring that domestic retail prices remained largely stable despite international crises.

Inspecting petrol pumps in Indore on Sunday, the Rajya Sabha member from Madhya Pradesh said the Centre had cut excise duty three times, in November 2021, May 2022 and March 10, 2026, limiting the rise in fuel prices in India to "around seven per cent against a 50-70 per cent surge globally".
PM Modi's policies protected Indians from global fuel price shocks, he told reporters.

He also praised state-run oil marketing companies Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) for "absorbing heavy losses" when crude oil prices rose from $60-65 to $120 per barrel.
Dismissing the Opposition's claims about shortage of petrol, diesel and cooking gas amid the Iran conflict as baseless rumours, the minister said supplies remained uninterrupted across the country.
"Not a single one of our 1,07,000 retail outlets experienced a dry-out.
During the last Parliament session, our political friends welcomed me with gas cylinder cutouts, claiming an imminent crisis and that LPG cylinders had run out.
"Yet, there was no shortage anywhere because we ramped up domestic LPG production," he said.

stories.headline: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water
stories.title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 22: Food regulator FSSAI on Sunday said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after finding its sample of packaged drinking water "unsafe". In a social media post, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water". A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis. "The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said. Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added. The findings of the lab established violations relating to unsafe food under the law. Hence, the FSSAI said it has granted sanction to launch prosecution under the FSS Act, 2006, against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd. During this calendar year, the FSSAI has stepped up enforcement actions against food business operators as well as e-commerce companies. The regulator has also cracked down on energy drink and alcoholic beverage makers.
